h1:
Walking Phrae's Old Town
City Walls, Teak Houses, Ancient Temples & Quiet Cafés
intro: Phrae's old town is compact enough to cover on foot in a single day. Inside a snail-shaped ancient moat — sections of which are still visible — you'll find Pratu Chai as the landmark gateway, the century-old Khum Chao Luang palace and pink teak mansion, a cluster of walkable temples showcasing northern Thai craftsmanship, and cafés in genuinely old wooden houses so quiet you can hear the breeze. Here's a complete walking route with real opening hours and admission prices.

blocks.html: Most visitors drive straight through Phrae on the way to Nan — but step into the In Wiang quarter inside the ancient walls and you'll find something rare: whole teak houses still standing, walkable temples within minutes of each other, and coffee shops that aren't just styled for photos but actually occupy old wooden homes. The best part? Everything is within easy walking distance so you won't spend the day circling for parking.

Phrae's historic centre sits inside a spiral-shell-shaped earthen moat — still visible along several stretches — with temples, old noble residences, a market, and cafés all clustered inside. One loop takes you past almost everything.

blocks.text: Start at Pratu Chai — the Old Town's Landmark Gateway

blocks.html: Pratu Chai is one of the surviving city gates and the natural starting point for any walk through In Wiang. The red-brick walls set a distinctly ancient mood and look great in photos at both midday and the softer late-afternoon light. Around the gate you'll find the municipal market and local food stalls — a good spot to grab something before you start walking.

blocks.title: Where to park
blocks.html: If you're driving, find a spot near Khum Chao Luang or around Pratu Chai and explore on foot from there. Many streets inside the old town are narrow and one-way, so walking is genuinely faster than circling by car.

blocks.title: Want more out of Phrae? Book tours & activities
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Phrae
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Khum Chao Luang + The Pink Teak Mansion

blocks.html: At the heart of the old town stand two noble residences you shouldn't skip. Both are built entirely from teak and showcase the "gingerbread" style — Thai-European hybrid architecture with delicately carved wooden fretwork.

items.name: Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae
items.blurb: The former residence of Phiria Therawong, the last ruling lord of Phrae, built in 1892. Now the Phrae City Museum, free to enter. The two-storey structure with a high ground floor features rooms displaying Phrae's history and period artefacts.

items.name: Baan Wongburi (The Pink House)
items.blurb: A century-old pink teak mansion built in 1897, still furnished with the original noble family's belongings. Admission around 30 THB. The image most people picture when they think of Phrae.

blocks.html: The two houses are only a few hundred metres apart. We recommend visiting mid-morning when the light is flattering for photos against the warm-toned wood.

blocks.title: Free tram tour of the old town
blocks.html: Khum Chao Luang also offers a free tram ride around the old town, passing multiple temples and historic wooden houses — roughly an hour. Worth checking if it's running the day you visit, as schedules can vary. Good option for a scorching afternoon when walking feels like too much.

blocks.text: Ancient Temples Inside the Walls — All Walkable

blocks.html: One of Phrae's great advantages is that its ancient temples sit inside the old town and you can walk between them without needing a vehicle. Each one has something different: carved wooden viharn halls, old chedis, and original northern Thai craftsmanship.

items.name: Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang Worawihan
items.blurb: The city's central temple, enshrining Phra Phuttha Kosai Siri Chai Maha Sakyamuni — Phrae's most revered Buddha image. The golden Ming Mueang chedi is hard to miss, and the temple is right in the heart of the old quarter.

items.name: Wat Phong Sunan
items.blurb: A beautiful temple close to the pink mansion, with a gilded chedi and an intricate glass-mosaic viharn. Conveniently next to Kad Kong Kao market — easy to combine with Baan Wongburi.

items.name: Wat Chom Sawan
items.blurb: A Shan (Tai Yai) style temple with a genuinely old teak viharn, tiered roofline in the Burmese-Shan tradition, and rare ivory manuscripts and antiques inside. The architecture stands apart from every other temple in the city.

items.name: Wat Sara Bo Kaew
items.blurb: Best visited at dusk when the illuminations come on. The ordination hall and chedi feature refined stucco work, and it pairs well with an evening stroll to Kad Kong Kao market right after.

items.name: Wat Phra Non
items.blurb: An old town temple with a large reclining Buddha and an aged wooden viharn. Mostly visited by locals rather than tourists, keeping the atmosphere genuinely calm.
items.meta: Within the old town walls · Free entry

blocks.title: What to wear at the temples
blocks.html: Most temples in the old town are free and are active places of worship for local residents. Cover your shoulders and wear trousers or a skirt below the knee. Remove shoes before entering any wooden viharn.

blocks.text: Slow Cafés in Old Wooden Houses

blocks.html: Rest your legs at one of the old town's wooden-house cafés. Phrae has several coffee spots in genuinely old timber buildings — rarely crowded, and well suited to sitting out a hot afternoon. The picks below are all within the walking route, easy to drop into after a temple or two.

items.name: Slope Coffee (Baan Beaw)
items.blurb: A café inside a genuinely tilting old wooden house — "beaw" means slanted in Northern Thai dialect. Decorated with vintage pieces, old frames, and school-style wooden tables. The back garden under a large tree is very quiet. Located on Thanon Kham Lue in the Kad Kong Kao area, walkable from Baan Wongburi.
items.meta: Thanon Kham Lue, Kad Kong Kao · Open approx. 9:00–18:00 (later on Saturdays)

items.name: Cher Bar
items.blurb: A small, easygoing café on Thanon Kham Lue, right next to Wat Phong Sunan. Perfectly positioned on the walking route — stop for a coffee straight after the temple.
items.meta: Thanon Kham Lue, next to Wat Phong Sunan

items.name: Ho: Bake & Craft Café
items.blurb: A warm, homey café on the road encircling the In Wiang quarter. House-baked pastries, relaxed atmosphere — easy to linger here.
items.meta: Ring road, In Wiang · Open approx. 9:00–16:00

items.name: Charlotte Hut Coffee & Tea Bar
items.blurb: A central Phrae café in the In Wiang area, open from morning to evening. Works well for an early breakfast before setting out or an afternoon break mid-walk.

blocks.title: Small café hours vary
blocks.html: Many wooden-house cafés in the old town are owner-operated. Opening days and hours can shift, especially around public holidays. Worth checking their Facebook page before making a special trip to a specific spot.

blocks.text: Friday–Saturday Evenings: Kad Kong Kao Night Market

blocks.html: If you're here on a Friday or Saturday, wrap up the day at Kad Kong Kao — Phrae's walking street along Thanon Kham Lue, close to Baan Wongburi and Wat Phong Sunan. It runs from late afternoon to around 21:00, with northern Thai street food, souvenirs, local textiles, and roadside coffee stalls. Strolling and snacking with old wooden shophouses on both sides is an ideal way to close the day.

items: When it runs — mostly Friday–Saturday evenings, approx. 16:00–21:00. Double-check if you're visiting around a public holiday.
Food highlights — Kanom Jeen Nam Ngiao, Khao Kap (rice crackers), Sai Oua sausage, and northern Thai desserts.
Souvenirs — Mor Hom indigo-dyed cloth, Phrae's most distinctive product, sold throughout the market.

blocks.text: How to Cover Everything in One Day

blocks.html: Every spot in the old town is within walking distance of the others. Here's a route that gets through the highlights comfortably, starting in the morning and finishing after dark.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Teak mansions and the city's main temple

items.activity: Breakfast coffee at Charlotte Hut or Ho: Bake & Craft
items.note: Fuel up before the walk — pick whichever is closer to your accommodation in In Wiang.

items.activity: Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae (museum, free entry)
items.note: Ask at the reception about the free tram tour schedule while you're here.

items.activity: Baan Wongburi — the pink teak mansion
items.note: Admission around 30 THB. A short walk from Khum Chao Luang.

items.activity: Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang — the city's main temple
items.note: Pay respects to Phrae's most revered Buddha image.

items.activity: Lunch — local northern Thai food in the In Wiang area
items.note: Kanom Jeen Nam Ngiao or a local rice shop inside the old quarter.

items.activity: Wat Chom Sawan + Wat Phong Sunan
items.note: Admire the Shan-style teak viharn, then walk on to the ornate temple near the pink mansion.

items.activity: Coffee break at Slope Coffee (Baan Beaw)
items.note: Sit in the back garden — the quietest spot in the old town on a sunny afternoon.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.title: Temple lights and the night market

items.activity: Wat Sara Bo Kaew as the lights come on
items.note: Catch the temple in the soft pre-dark light before full illumination.

items.activity: Kad Kong Kao walking street (Friday–Saturday only)
items.note: Stroll, eat local street food, and pick up some Mor Hom cloth as a souvenir.
If the market doesn't align with your trip dates, come here instead for atmospheric photos of the old gate after dark.

blocks.title: Only have half a day?
blocks.html: Three stops cover the essence: Khum Chao Luang + Baan Wongburi + Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang, finished with a coffee in one wooden-house café. That's enough to get a real feel for Phrae's old town.

faq.q: How long does it take to walk Phrae's old town?
faq.a: At a relaxed pace with photo stops and a café break, expect 6–8 hours for a full day. If you only have half a day, the trio of Khum Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, and Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang still gives a genuine taste of the old quarter — everything is within easy walking distance.

faq.q: Is there an admission fee for the teak mansions and temples?
faq.a: Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae is free. Baan Wongburi (the pink house) charges around 30 THB. Most temples inside the old town walls are free to enter; donations are welcome.

faq.q: When does Kad Kong Kao night market run?
faq.a: Kad Kong Kao is a walking street on Thanon Kham Lue that typically runs Friday–Saturday evenings, roughly 16:00–21:00. If you're planning around the market, aim for Saturday to be safe.

faq.q: Is there a city tour if I'd rather not walk the whole route?
faq.a: Yes — Khum Chao Luang offers a free tram ride around the old town, covering several temples and historic wooden houses in about an hour. Check the schedule at the venue when you arrive as it can change day to day.

faq.q: Which café in the old town is the quietest for sitting a while?
faq.a: Slope Coffee (Baan Beaw) has a back garden under a large tree that's genuinely peaceful. Cher Bar and Ho: Bake & Craft are also within the walking route and have a calm, unhurried atmosphere — good for a long afternoon sit.
